t: Bring 5 portions of mad mushroom pulp to Shot the Sober at the Imperial Outpost, brew mushroom wine and treat the five aviak sentries and watchers.

The world has two universal languages, the one is spoken by tongue, the other is understood by mind...
Harpoon has already spoken the first universal language to the red-feathered, and everyone has seen the result. The second language can be understood using a versatile translator, so to say... I'm preparing it right now. Judging by the latest news, we'll need more than one barrel of the translator to send our birdies to battle.
A true alchemist can always find materials to work with. Back on campus of our institute for alchemy and magic technology, we'd even use stools to make potions. Of all the raw materials I tried around here, mushroom pulp is the best. See them crawling around the camp? Crush them, gut them and bring the pulp here. Any questions? I'll cook it quick, and you'll feed our nestlings. This may even improve our relationship!
Aviaks and I tried various compositions, and now my tongue's out of control.
Yes, that's better. Peace, friends, hiccups! As I went home on Monday night as drunk as drunk could be...
Collect 10 lianas around the Imperial Outpost and bring them to Zuu Addle-Pate.

Why did I become a ropemaker? Everyone says, making rope does not need much brain. If you're lazy or stupid, people say - you are a ropemaker, not warrior. What about me? The work's easy, no need to fight, no need to carry heavy things. Sit here, spin rope, no sweat, and you look busy.
But this new lift causes me gazillion troubles! Bring the weight up, bring the weight down, lift the wingless ones, change the rope every hour! I don't have time to make rope! Blisters on all fingers! Why did they take me on military campaign? Mosquitoes bite! I am tired! Don't wanna be here!
Hey, you, wingless one! Go up-down? Wearing my rope out? Go bring me lianas for a new rope, many lianas! Otherwise it'll break again, but I don't have a new rope ready!
I look at the camp, I think - between wingless one and a ropemaker, a ropemaker is smarter!
Good liana, strong! Hey, wingless one! Wanna be my student? Be an assistant ropemaker, bring lianas all day!
I know nothing about Crystal Mountain, Marai-Nui! A terrible place! Forbidden! One who asks questions is more inane than me, worse than a ropemaker! Stupid, stupid like Ulumi Half-Wing!
h: Ask about the mountain in the north

t: Yes, wingless? Do you want to know how to make rope?
Explore the mound and find the reason for the shaman's madness.

Born on the Isle of Singing Water, near Decrepit Mound. A famous healer, a cook by calling. A farmer among people and a fisher at sea. So to say, necessary in magic. That's the system, so to speak. Amounting to two hundred units. One can see Decrepit Mound and get a crech-tech karrach. And a warrior works as a cook. Because there's no air, there's a shaman. One can see Decrepit Mound and become the air master, like an air allod"...
The old shaman is talking nonsense, constantly repeating something about the Decrepit Mound. Is he talking about the big mound at the heart of the Cape of Chiefs? There's a point in going there: maybe that's the place where something happened to Aikho that made him lose his mind.

Among the ancient mossy stones, there stands an idol, once brightly painted but now faded. It had been deserted years ago, but, judging by the fresh coals and splashes of blood, some ritual was held here not long ago.
Collect 7 pieces of Brushwood and obtain 13 rhinoceros' Sacrificial Hearts at the Cape of Chiefs and make a sacrifice on top of the Decrepit Mound.

One of the rocks was carefully cleaned from moss and dirt. Some pictograms are engraved on it, they look like a primal manual on how to use a sacrificial altar. Looks like Aikho held that ritual but could not come to terms with what he summoned. There is only one solution: repeat the ritual, summon the spirit who punished the shaman and make him dispel his curse.
The pictographic manual is much easier to understand than most manuals for Imperial household magic appliances. These are obviously a big bowl and a fire. That's logical: no sacrifice without fire. This is some animal. Judging by a horn on its nose it must be a rhinoceros. Several small hearts are carved next to it, a dozen and one in number, and a symbolic fire once again. This is unlikely to mean some ardent love of animals but rather the thirteen hearts burned on the altar.
Well, let's make an offering and see who comes running at the smell of burning flesh.
Only fools would awaken a shadow of the past, one fool after another...
Survive Chief Arikee's anger and defeat his ghost in combat.
Unworthy descendants! Do you want a war? Do you want the dead to spill blood of the alive? Then be it so!
Wait... You're not the one of our People... You're not dead... Who are you?
Kill 10 monkeys and their leader at the Cape of Chiefs, take the ritual gourd and bring it to Ghost of Chief Arikee on the Decrepit Mound.

Listen to me, outlander. I lived and did great things, and died long, long time ago. I cleansed the jungle so People could have place to live. I killed a monstrous octopus so that People could go fishing. I invented a chopper, a rope, a flint to make fire in the fireplace and drums for dancing. I died and slept in peace, and People burned early fruits and sweet meat in memory of Arikee.
Then People became foolish. A brother ripped a brother, and a wing went to war against another wing, and People became two tribes. The path to my grave grew over, old songs were forgotten, everything was for the war, for the victory. And I cried in my grave. Then, big darkness came from the outside, killed both tribes. I was old, wise and dead, I knew the outcome. Unworthy descendants did not know and they continued their war, although they all were dead for a long time. And then a stupid shaman came here, summoned my spirit and asked me to help the Steel Claw in the war against the White Wing! I did not know if I should laugh or weep! I punished that fool and scattered his brains all over the forest.
So you outlander are fighting a big rotting god who lives beyond the world and want to help that old fool? Well, I can forgive the shaman if you complete my task.
First, find a sacred ritual gourd. They used to carry sweet wine, then they forgot about it, and it was stolen by monkeys. Take the sacred gourd from monkeys. And punish filthy animals, teach them never mess on my grave again!
Brain serves old shaman poorly, looks like he does not need it at all.
I remember this gourd. No one fill it with fragrant wine for me any more. Well, let's fill it with thoughts of the old fool.
Collect 10 Wild Orchids, 12 Crocodile Teeth and 12 Crocodile Scales at the Cape of Chiefs and bring them to Ghost of Chief Arikee on the Decrepit Mound.

Old sacrificial gourd can hold brain fragments, but can the outlander's eye see? Don't worry. Chief Arikee gives People much knowledge and skills for all occasions. I invented potion making. Now I'll give you the recipe of the potion that helps see brain fragments.
The first component of that potion is orchid flowers. The second component is a crocodile, its sharp teeth and hard scales. Bring everything to me, I'll make the potion.
A tooth must have a dent like this, otherwise it won't do. Not all scale are good either, only scales with this pattern. Orchid is not the major component, so any orchid will do.
Grind the tooth, grate the scales, press the flower sap... That's it. Apply this potion onto your eyes and see brain fragments.

Apply the ointment of enlightenment to see Aikho's brain fragments wandering around the forest on the Cape of Chiefs. Weaken the fragment's in battle and use the ritual gourd to imprison its essence. Collect 6 fragments and restore the brain to Aikho Three-Eyed.

Now you can see and catch old fool's brain fragments. The last step is to find them and force them into the gourd. This good, strong brain hardly wants to return into a stupid head. When you see a brain fragment, beat it until it gives in and hide it in the gourd at once.
I'll return to my sleep now. I'm sick at soul for all that happens, but I am dead and this song is no longer about me.
Outlander, you see our People vanish, destroyed by folly and endless feud. People would not even raise choppers to protect from great darkness: the Glittering Wing is busy beating the Steel Claw, and the Steel Claw is busy fighting the Glittering Wing. Your song is not over yet, outlander. May you learn from the one whose song is over. May heaven help you outlander in fight against rotting god. Farewell.
Do you know Ko'Chuck have a bump right under the beak?
Ka... Kharr! What happened? Where is Aikho Three-Eyed? Who are you wingless one?

Use the talisman of Aikho Three-Eyed in three places of the Imperial Outpost: in the place of Shorr's death, in the tent where Harpoon was killed, and near the aviak witnesses. Return with the talisman to Aikho on the Cape of Chiefs.

Did you speak with chief Arikee? What did the chief say? That's how it is, then... I admit: he's really an old worthless fool. Thank you, wingless one, for giving me his stupid brain back.
So, why did you wingless one look for Aikho? Krakk! Evil spirit! I cannot leave the village for an instance, as something bad happens the next moment every time!
No time to panic, we need to be reasonable. Sure, the proletarian intuition is strong in commander Schorr, but we need to check everything again. Here's the talisman, it can sense traces of spirits. Take it where the evil spirit showed up: where Shorr was murdered, where the possessed orc died, and where the murder eyewitnesses were. If that's truly an evil spirit, the talisman will record traces. If not, then even a proletarian intuition fails at times.
Red-winged commander smells both enemy and treason, but I doubt that he senses an evil spirit.

I confess: evil spirit was here. A strong, bright trace of the commander. A weak, but reeking trace of a witness. Possessed... Oh, the stench made me dizzy. Didn't look like a living being, so twisted and nasty, like an evil spirit.
How strange. There is another trace on the talisman... Guess who? You! Your trace, not stinky, but very similar to the evil spirit's trace! Like you are coming down the same path. Maybe it's you who brought the evil spirit to our land?
Ask Semer Nifuni for advice at the Imperial Outpost.

I've probably lost my mind. It's time to change my name to Aikho the Brainless. I lived a long life, I've worked magic so many years, but I've never seen things like what happened recently. What advice can I offer my wingless guest? Just one thing - even the most powerful evil spirit is not invincible. Evil must be punished. Like every secret is revealed one day, any spirit can become a target for a true hand and a pure heart. But how to beat a spirit that follows you wingless one, only you will know best.
For Aikho wingless people are strange, a mystery. Young and handsome, but ancient and dead. Smells like grave, but has great will to live. One speaks a lot, female, name of Sem-mer-ni-fu-ni. Has mind clear like spring, sharp like arrowhead. If anyone know how to beat spirit, she know. Go, tell her what I say. Aikho believe you can do well.
Have you caught up with Aikho Three-Eyed? He's a peculiar oldster, but quite sharp. What did he tell you?
Meet Harpoon the Brassbound to find out about the circumstances of the murder. Report to Alexander Vertiankin at the Imperial Outpost.

Don't move! From this moment and until we clarify all the circumstances, you are under arrest. What circumstances? Don't be smart!
Oh, you don't know? Don't know nothing, didn't see nothing? OK, I will remind you about a couple of facts. Last night you were seen with Harpoon the Brassbound, you were discussing something with him. Ten minutes after your conversation, Harpoon attacked Commander Shorr and sent him to the Purgatory. What do you have to say for yourself?
You say that you weren't here last night? But you could've used the lift... What do you mean, it's broken?! Can someone confirm that? Crow the Riverborn, Kibal Chikhun and Cha Pie-Pie himself? Yeah, well, it does seem that you have a strong alibi. Then who was seen with the murderer last night?
You know what, let's have a confrontation. We'll question the both of you, and see what lies each of you tells.
Harpoon is in that tent. Come on, it's time for the interrogation.
What does that mean? Who gave you the right to execute the suspect before a court verdict?
Complete the tasks given by Sookie Dry-Wing, Shot the Sober and Zuu Addle-Pate, then report to Alexander Vertiankin at the Imperial Outpost.

Who do you think you are? Do you think that being a Hero of the Empire gives you the right to pass sentences and execute prisoners, especially while they're under investigation?!
Hmm... So, you claim that he attacked you and this was self-defense? Well, perhaps that's true. But this still looks very suspicious. You have an alibi, but you were seen. It seems as though you have nothing to hide, but the only person who could confirm that is dead and gone. Liters? Oh, come on. How many liters would you have to drink to start attacking your own? What does Tep have to do with this? How about Gorluxor - did he set you up? Hah!
The trouble is that, even if you really have been framed, it's no help to us. I believe you, as you are an honored Hero of the Empire and all, but aviaks don't exactly read our newspapers. The way they see it is simple - a wingless foreigner went and killed their commander for no reason. They are scared of us now. Not to mention the invasion which can happen any day!
Listen, let's do this. I will leave Harpoon's death on your conscience. We'll write it off as a war casualty. But you'll have to sort out the consequences anyway. You must regain the aviaks' trust, or we will lose this campaign before even the first battle is fought.
Aviaks would do anything for their commander. They won't forgive his death so easily. Even if he's already been resurrected.
Shorr's Deputy has flown by just now with an invitation to have a drink of firewater with the commander and discuss the plan of attack. Nice work!
Obtain spores of the Furious Mushroom and bring them to Shot the Sober at the Imperial Outpost.

Instead of going hunting every day, it would be much easier to start my own mushroom patch. I've already tried to sow spores, but they don't grow up. Nothing grows there, despite all my efforts.
But don't be in despair. You know what I mean - we should not give up! I saw an amazing mushroom in the forest the other day, at least as tall as me. I am no mushroom specialist, but I suspect the spores from this mushroom should be equally huge. We'll start a proper mushroom garden - then we'll have both drinks and snacks always at hand! How's that for a plan?
Just don't go looking for that mushroom alone. Like I said, it's huge, angry and quite aggressive. Bring some friends with you, the tougher the better.
Our teacher taught us that spores begot all life. But I can't even grow a simple mushroom!
Oh, just you look at that! They are trying to bite my finger - how cool is that? If they come up, I'll make delicious mushroom wine out of 'em.
Well, how are your negotiations with the aviaks going?
Have you spilt it? No problem, I've got some more here, at the bottom of it.
Oh, that's just what I needed! Give it here, let's get started.
h: Here's the mushroom pulp for the tincture

t: Where is it, I wonder... ha! Wine is a strange thing - one moment it's here, and the next it's all gone. I know what we need - mushrooms! Go get some more, and I'll cook 'em up.
Question Schorr Fly-by-Shore about the circumstances of his death.

Gracious sir, may I steal a few minutes of your precious time? I have an incredibly important matter for your consideration. I am one of the guerillas fighting to oppose the tyranny of the architect of these dreams, so to speak. Do forgive me, I can't tell you my name right now, but the Resistance calls me the Ghost.
Our common friend sent you to look for holes in the fabric of this grand illusion. Your search has already been interrupted twice by extraordinarily curious, albeit frightening creatures. Let us call them Lictors. They are the executioners of the master who has woven the fabric of this delusion, and he does not want his creation to be ripped by those caught in it. Within the boundaries of this illusory world they can wield any power that their creator endowed onto them.
It would seem that they are invincible, wouldn't it? That may be, but let me draw your attention to a rather curious paradox. To protect the fabric of reality from holes, even a concocted reality, they must be interwoven in it themselves. That means that, by virtue of their service, they are restricted by the rules and laws of this world... It follows that they must also have a certain weakness.
There is just one thing left to do, a simple little thing - find that weakness and learn to use it against them. Let's pull on the only thread that we have. Question that poor aviak about how he was killed by a Lictor. Perhaps his story will give us a clue.
Bad things happen here. Very bad.

This is a bad story. It shivers me feathers, so bad. First, warriors saw you with the killer, confirmed everything. But no way you could be there then. Do you know what old men say about those who appear in two places at one time? Old men say - they are evil spirits! Youngsters laugh, but it's not funny.
Second, the killer was not drunk, and was not mad either. I saw how men went mad in war. No, no, it's not what happens here. The oc was like a doll, moved like strings were tied to his arms. Eyes like glass, voice like rusty lift. He talked stupid things. Many numbers and something about memory that can't be read. Orc shouted that my team was bad and my name was bad, then he attacked me!
And three. I don't want to show off, but I know I can't be beaten by a fighter like an orc with even with my wings tied behind my back. But he killed me in one blow! Bam, and I went to a big dark room with a big door. How did that happen?
They think old people tell stories, but my senses are strong. This was an evil spirit, for sure.
Well, what did the aviak say? Are there any other... clues, if you will?
Find Aikho Three-Eyed on the Cape of Chiefs.

Hmm, what can I say... It's exactly as I suspected. The Architect didn't damage his creation by introducing strange unbeatable creatures. Instead, he carefully wove them into the fabric of his creation as evil spirits. They manipulate events by putting up obstacles in the saboteurs' path, while keeping the world's logic unharmed. Evil spirits can get away with quite a lot, for the common folk are used to blaming all their troubles on them... But then they are also accustomed to looking for ways to beat them, right?
I think that we need to find us a specialist on evil spirits. Like any self-respecting tribe, Steel Claw must have a shaman. His name is Aikho Three-Eyed, and he's got quite a unique view of the world. If a spirit has left its mark on the victim's aura, as is usually the case, the shaman will be able to see it.
Right now he is gone to the Cape of Chiefs on some important matters. Of course, you realize that this matter is no less important. Catch up with Aikho and ask him for help before you encounter another Lictor, or worse...
I am like an old decrepit mound, quickly, hurry to dig me up...
Collect 8 Astral Monocrystals in the mine and bring them to Semer Nifuni at the Imperial Outpost.

The extent to which primitive myths and legends can preclude and even overtake scientific progress is simply amazing. Did he sing for you the Song of the White Cloud? I could take whole stanzas from there and insert them into my manuscript on the control of immaterial substances. In fact, that's exactly what I'm planning on doing when we return.
So, what did old Aikho tell you? Ah, OK. An atypical ethereal entity, danger level Red. We have encountered these creatures in Lab No...However, you don't need to know that. I can recreate the device that we used to close the breach, but I will need a working body. Crystals... We need astral monocrystals - the kind that hang off allod bottoms like clusters of grape, only smaller. Lucky for us, Junes have left a crystal mine nearby. I've seen samples from there, and those crystals will be perfect for our task. I will need eight of them, one for each cardinal direction. Go get them while I put the device together.
You need to hurry. If that spirit is what I think it is, you're not going to want to meet him without a weapon.

Just beautiful. None of the Imperial mines produce crystals of this size and purity. And neither do the League ones, according to our sources. That's it, the device is ready. But I can't give it to you just yet. It will help you to find the ethereal entity and force it to materialize, but even in that state the spirits of that class are incredibly dangerous. You won't stand a chance in a fair battle. You must find a special weapon. Alas, that is not my area of expertise. Try asking the aviaks for advice. As I've said before, their primitive shamanism sometimes overtakes even the latest scientific discoveries and cutting-edge magic technologies.
Kill 15 Stone Elementals in the Abandoned Mine and report to Alexander Vertiankin at the Imperial Outpost.

Here is the order. International duty is important, to be sure, but we must not forget about our own country. Since we've already introduced a limited contingent of Imperial troops to the Windy Hills, it would make sense to survey the area for strategic resources.
Our valiant scouts have discovered an ancient mine in the southern part of the island. Judging by its architectural style, this construction is much older than either the whites or the reds. In fact, it looks like the work of Junes. True, our scouts didn't come upon any June mechanisms, but the mine is full of native crystals!
I'm sure the League is already plotting a way to get their paws on this treasure. Our objective is to beat them to it. A team of goblin miners is ready to start mining. Unfortunately, stone elementals have made their home in that mine as well. Your task is to ensure safe working conditions for our miners. Destroy at least a dozen elementals.

The Imperial Labor Code clearly states - hazardous and dangerous factors at the worksite must be eliminated or, at the very least, reduced to a minimum. Have you managed to reduce the number of stone elementals in the mine to an acceptable level?
Were safe working conditions provided for the glory of the Motherland? That's great. I'll deploy the brigade.
Obtain 20 Tapir Skins near the mine and bring them to Sookie Dry-Wing at the Imperial Outpost.

White masters take seven skins from poor peasants. How to survive? I know, to protect your skin, you need armor made from another's skin. Strong, powerful animals has tough skin. I will tan, scrape, make a strong armor. I just need raw materials.
There are big-nosed animals near a big hole in the ground. Their skin is tough, nothing can be better. Can the Empire fulfill its international duty, help their aviak comrades? Obtain twenty skins and bring them to me.
Steel Claw suffers under the burden of the white-winged! Where is help from your developed nation?
This will make a good armor - no spear or blade or arrow will cut it. The Empire is a good ally.
Find a Lictor in the Muggy Jungle by using the detector and defeat it with the Spear of Truth.

Let me have a look at that spear... Clearly, there was a good reason to sign you up for the expedition. Not everyone can knock together an ethereal entity disintegrator from sticks and stone. Take the detector. Let me just explain its theory and application...
The detector is tuned to the entity which has caused you so much grief. It's nesting somewhere in the northern part of the island, in the Muggy Jungle. You can't miss its lair - there's a significant reality distortion around it. When the target is very close, press this button. It will switch on the distorting contour, forcing the spirit to materialize. I've said it before and I'll say it again - it will be very tough and dangerous. Don't even try to take it on with regular weapons or magic - they can only weaken it to a point when you can use the spear. Do you understand? Good. Then there is just one thing I can say to you.
Good luck!
Fantastic! Truly, nothing can stop someone who believes in himself!

So, you've managed to obtain... well, to create... a weapon capable of destroying the elite servants of Tep - the Lictors. Congratulations! What do you think has really defeated your enemy? The logic of the world, perhaps the rules of the game that he must obey? Correct. But that's just one side of the truth.
Do you remember what you had to do to acquire this spear? You've passed some kind of test, haven't you? You have shown the will to win, so to speak, by opposing oblivion. That's why this spear is more than just some imagined toy in the illusory world. In a manner of speaking, this weapon is the manifestation of your will to live. If my theory is correct, it will remain with you in the real world, where it will just as dangerous to the architect of dreams as it is here.
Kill 15 mosquitoes near the Imperial Outpost and report to Sookie Dry-Wing.

Parasites! Blood suckers! How long will they drink blood of working aviaks!
No, I don't mean the white-winged now. I mean ordinary blood suckers. When it's hot, whole army of mosquitoes rises up from the swamp. Buzz, buzz, feast on poor ones suffering! They drink and drink, and it's never enough, they swell but never burst. Soon they'll be as big as an aviak and still want more!
Fighting with mosquitoes is like whipping sea. But we have do something. Near the camp, whack ten or more fat mosquitoes that threaten not health but life.
Be brave,hero! I heard you rid Empire of blood suckers - now help the Steel Claw!
Sookie hear buzz stop. Good! It be good if white feather do it too...
Bring 5 portions of mad mushroom pulp to Shot the Sober at the Imperial Outpost, brew mushroom wine and treat five aviak sentries and observers.

The world has two universal languages, the one is spoken by tongue, the other is understood by mind...
Harpoon has already spoken the first universal language to the red-feathered, and everyone has seen the result. The second language can be understood using a versatile translator, so to say... I'm preparing it right now. Judging by the latest news, we'll need more than one barrel of the translator to send our birdies to battle.
A true alchemist can always find materials to work with. Back on campus of our institute for alchemy and magic technology, we'd even use stools to make potions. Of all the raw materials I tried around here, mushroom pulp is the best. See them crawling around the camp? Crush them, gut them and bring the pulp here. Any questions? I'll cook it quick, and you'll feed our nestlings. This may even improve our relationship!
Aviaks and I tried various compositions, and now my tongue's out of control.
Patriotism, courage, readiness to die for the Motherland - I have a recipe for everything. Just bring me raw materials!
Collect 10 lianas around the Imperial Outpost and bring them to Zuu Addle-Pate.

Why did I become a ropemaker? Everyone says, making rope does not need much brain. If you're lazy or stupid, people say - you are a ropemaker, not warrior. What about me? The work's easy, no need to fight, no need to carry heavy things. Sit here, spin rope, no sweat, and you look busy.
But this new lift causes me gazillion troubles! Bring the weight up, bring the weight down, lift the wingless ones, change the rope every hour! I don't have time to make rope! Blisters on all fingers! Why did they take me on military campaign? Mosquitoes bite! I am tired! Don't wanna be here!
Hey, you, wingless one! Go up-down? Wearing my rope out? Go bring me lianas for a new rope, many lianas! Otherwise it'll break again, but I don't have a new rope ready!
I look at the camp, I think - between wingless one and a ropemaker, a ropemaker is smarter!
Good liana, strong! Hey, you wingless! Want be Zuu student? Be assistant rope maker, bring liana all day!
Return to Kahlua Island and ask Elchana how to defeat the evil spirit.

I don't know how to fight an evil spirit. The Steel Claw does not fear anyone from flesh and bone, but how to fight an enemy with no body?
Warriors think the evil spirit is the old wives' tale. So, an old wife should be asked for advice. Go to Kahlua Island. An ancient old witch lives there, Elchana Speak-with-Spirist. Elchana knows the recipe for any circumstance, she can advise how to kill the spirit.
Son of the Wind came again... White in face, worry in heart. I know how to help.
Kill 15 Pagan Aviaks or Sermoners of the Church of Light, then report to Elchana Speak-with-Spirits on Kahlua island.

Now this s-s-s-spear can banish the spirits of lies-s-s-s... Jus-s-s-s-t have to prove that you des-s-s-serve to own it. Show me, s-s-s-s... how you des-s-s-troy your enemies-s-s-s. Then I'll dec-c-c-cide whether you have the s-s-s-strength to battle the enemies-s-s-s of this world...

Everyone wants to believe that he's on the side of truth and his enemy isn't. But there is only one truth in the war between the Glittering Wing and the Steel Claw, as in the war between the League and the Empire - you truly hate and want to destroy each other. That is not scary. That is the way of our world - it's fueled by fighting.
You have proved you have power to fix what's broken. I'll give you this spear. Go and exorcise the evil spirits.
Ask Semer Nifuni at the Imperial Camp for help.

Now the warriors are armed! But can a warrior see? Does a warrior know how to find enemy, how to sneak up to him, how to strike? Evil spirit is slippery, untouchable like smoke and shadows.
You need help to fight the spirit of falsehood. Not mine, no - you already know the one who can help, you arrived on the same ship! A woman that came to know death early and became united with it. The voice of reason that sounds from under a burial mask. Go to her, ask for help. She will grant you the sight!

There are certainly many folk beliefs and practices that still await a dedicated researcher. Though the sorceress has never seen me, referring you to me was right on the nose. If you already have a weapon against an immaterial entity, I will help you to localize it.
Bring 4 Barrels of Explosives to the obstruction near Snake Waterfalls.

All right, listen up. Open your map and look here. This blotch in the center of the archipelago, crammed with miles and miles of rotting marches, is called the Windy Hills. What, don't feel like visiting? Well, too bad, 'cause you'll have to. For the moment it belongs to the white wings. They are backed by the League, and that means we'll be fighting for this worthless swampland as if it were a mine gushing meteorite! The brass has decided to help the red wings take over the marshes. An assault squadron has already been dispatched. They found a scrap of dry land, dug in and are now waiting for reinforcements... Except we can't send any! The League got wind of the attack and sabotaged our plans - they broke the lift and blocked the path. Now there's no way to get up there without wings.
But that's OK, 'cause if there's one thing they teach at the military command school is that any problem can be solved with enough explosives! And that we have plenty of... Well... We used to, at least.
Thing is, our brave boys were already carrying a load of explosives up here, but they landed in an anarchist ambush. We rushed to the rescue and did what we could, but it was too late... those reds that managed to survive bolted from the scene. After dropping all their loads, naturally. Luckily, the anarchists didn't have the chance to claim the spoils, so all those explosives are still in those bushes somewhere. I sent some goblins to look for them, but they are useless...
Maybe you'll have better luck? There were ten barrels in all. If you see any - grab it and bring it here!
If we don't recover enough explosives, we'll just have to do what Nezeb taught us - clear the way head on. As long as it's not my head!
One, two, three... Hey, we are four barrels short! I guess the anarchists grabbed 'em. What are we to do now?
Kill 10 Aviak Militants and Papa Riot near the Snake Waterfalls, then report to Crow the Riverborn.

What an inventive language! They are "anarchists," apparently. Back on the Wild Isles we just call them "rowdy." Nezeb only knows how many of them were killed before the Imperial authority was established. We wiped out whole clans, down to the last infant. But there will always be some smartass eager to hoist some colorful rag, band together a few like-minded knuckleheads, and declare their independence. "We do what we want, so bite us!" And we do! Bite them, that is. Chew them out, even, he he. I see that the aviaks have the same problem.
One such band is hanging around, wreaking havoc. Do I have to explain to you what needs to be done? And don't forget their ringleader! If you can't disperse them, we won't be able to lay a decent path to the top.
Well, how many nights longer will we need to endure their drunken singing?
Good, they had it coming. When you're fighting on two fronts simultaneously, you had best be ready to get hit on both.
Bring 15 portions of Wild Azalea Pump to Kibal Chikhun at the Snake Waterfalls.

Aye, the explosives are in short supply. Used most of 'em up already. I've got a bit stashed away, but it probably won't be enough. Although... I've got an idea...
Brisance... That's the shattering effect of the explosive, and it depends on a number of factors. The same substance can make a 'hiccup', a 'bam' or even a 'kaboom!', depending on how you grind it, press it, what you mix it with, how you detonate it... What, did you think a sapper's job was simple - just light the fuse and wait for your eyebrows to grow back?
Anyway, how much do we have left? Oh, that's enough for a detonation! Have you heard of explosive galantine? Don't worry if you haven't, you'll sleep better. My point is that, given the right substance, even two handfuls can be plenty. With a whole barrel there's enough to make a grand canyon. The problem is that all the right substances are back home, so we'll have to improvise.
Let's make use of the local plant life. There are flowers crawling around here. Gather a bucketful of their flesh and I will try to work a miracle.

Times like these make you appreciate the Divine Gift! Before it, the sapper couldn't afford even one mistake. But now a mistake simply means a time out to collect his brains and try to work out what he did wrong.
Hmm. The magician was drunk, and the trick failed. We need to find other materials... or use a different approach altogether.
Kill 8 Aviak Aanarchists and report to Alexander Vertiankin at the Imperial Outpost.

The map of the region has been scrawled on the parchment in ugly and uneven handwriting. That's the gorge, that's the Imperial Camp, that's the swamp... And what's that? You don't know how to read aviak scribbles, but skull and bones is a sign that doesn't need explanation, even when it's a bird skull. If the map is to be believed, there is a whole band of anarchists hiding right under the Imperials' noses!
It would be unwise to wait until they start causing trouble. On the contrary, they must be dealt with swiftly and efficiently, in accordance with martial law.
What have you got there? Some feathered artistic masterpiece? What?! The anarchists' map? Well, what are you waiting for? Go and check it!
Have you discovered and eliminated the anarchists' secret nest? Nice work! You are truly as good as they say.
Use Kibal Chikhun's rocket to fly up to the Windy Hills and secure a rope on the cliff. Report on your arrival to Alexander Vertiankin at the Imperial Outpost.

No, we won't be able to clear this mess any time soon. That's all right, there is always another way. You've always been drawn by the unknown, right? Wanted to conquer new challenges? Perhaps your inquisitive gaze has turned towards the depths of the Astral? Well, has it? Who are you trying to dupe - of course it has!
OK, listen up. There is a powder that makes flying real easy. And no, I am not talking about the powder that elves snort through a straw! I'm talking about proper, Imperial powder. If you light it, you'll get blown to another allod! I have put together this flying trinket out of the last bit of explosives. It's a prototype, but it works! Look, it even has handles for easier handling. Grab hold of it here, light it there, and kaboom! Next thing you know, you're looking down from a cliff. If you're lucky and my calculations are correct, you might even get there in one piece! Then you just toss down a rope, and we're good to go!
Well, what are you bellyaching about? Are you an Imperial soldier or what? Then off you go!
Just you look at this lack of discipline... Where are the promised reinforcements?
Look at what the cat dragged in. And we didn't even need a search party!
Extract 15 portions of Blacklip Snake Venom with your knife and bring them to Alk Two-Arrows.

I believe that Son of the Wind doesn't mean to. Sparring match can still be match, even old warrior's hand can slip, not moving sword fast enough. I'm old, I see many things and know lots about war. But a young warrior's like baby chick, not understands much. Son of the Wind, know this - they look on wingless one with respect and fear, they do not believe that you can make mistake.

Son of the Wind caused wound, now you must also help heal. Red-winged and wingless allies are strong, lots of attacks and injuries, but I'm lacking the healing balm. I need snake poison for balm. Go to forest, find the snake and kill it. Then be careful. Use this knife, cut it under tongue and drain poison. Don't drip on yourself, it's very dangerous! Bring me one dozen and three poison portions. Everyone will see how Son of the Wind cares for tribe, works for white wings' mission!
This poison is like a mature warrior. It can kill, or it can save.
You work quickly, you're a good hunter. Aviaks watch and learn. I se that you go hunting quite often.
Show combat moves to three aviaks and report to Voibor Ratov.

I'll be honest with you, the situation is quite bad. It's not just that we don't know where we are and how to get out of here, but now it has become obvious that all aspirations for peace with the Empire were the height of naivety. Even if Sarnaut were to be reduced to the size of one house, in one corner of which sat the last Imperial soldier, and in the other the last League solder... they would still be constantly at each other's throats. And, admittedly, I'd be just as likely to strike first. It's just... I hate them. I can't even express how much I hate them. For the Misty Slope, for Witch's Hollow, for all the ships that never returned home... And most of all - for yet another hope for peace and yet another betrayal.
But enough chitchat. Such is our disposition. Between us and the Imperial Outpost lies the Misty Hollow. The name sounds pretty, but it's actually a malaria-ridden swamp, well fertilized by the bodies of both white and red aviaks. And herein lies the problem - though the Children of the Wind are great warriors, they make pretty lousy soldiers. In the event of a battle, our white wings are sure to get all their feathers plucked. The Imperials understand that as well as we do, and I am sure they have already started to train and equip their red wings. And that means we'll have to do the same with ours.
Do you see the white-winged youngsters practicing over there? Go and show them some basic sparring techniques. But don't forget to adjust for claws and beaks!
Well, are our allies' beak sparring skills improving?
I will ask you very calmly and only once. What. The. Hell. Possessed. You. To. Kill. Him?
Collect 15 resilient branches from tropical treants and give them to Lada Vereskova. Then distribute 5 bows among the white-winged troopers.

I've never met archers quite as good as these locals. Just you look at what they are shooting from! It takes extraordinary skill to hit even a century-old oak with a bow of primitive stick-and-rope construction, let alone a moving target. It literally pains me to watch them struggle with that junk. If only we could give them something more practical than this sacred traditional ugliness...
Hold up, that's actually an idea. I am no armorer, but I made my first bow when I was five years old. Find me the right wood, such as from the treants from the local woods. Meanwhile, I'll make the bowstrings. To be safe, bring as many branches as you can. Even in skilled hands, branches have a tendency to break two times out of three.
I just saw some feathered super-genius shoot a bow with his feet. The funny part is that he hit the mark! If only they learn to do things properly, they would be unbeatable.

I am completely stunned. Our aviaks really liked the bows. They flew by, thanked us, praised the precision of the bows. But an hour later they were back playing with their old stick-and-rope weapons. Supposedly all the new bows broke. Or were lost. What do you call that, eh? Stubborn acts out of spite or plain old sabotage? We need to try and re-equip them again. When the Empire comes, these mighty birds will feel like helpless quails for all the good their tradition will do them.
Regain the aviaks' lost trust by completing their tasks and report to Voibor Ratov.

You are saying it was a Lector, eh? That is, an Imperial propagandist? So, he walked up to the aviaks, recited a lecture and convinced them to fall on the sword? Oh, was Tep there too? Or, perhaps, Nezeb himself, in person? That's not even funny. I don't want to listen to you anymore. One lie is worse than the other. There is nothing more pathetic in the world than a liar entangled in his own lies and scrambling for more. Have the courage to answer for your actions!
Honestly, I don't care how you happened to kill him - whether your hand slipped, or he was rude to you... That bastard has already been resurrected. The problem is that we've lost the aviaks' respect. As you have lost mine, by the way.
Now it's up to you to make things right. However you can. Wipe their floors, carry water from the well, I don't care - but for as long as they're still scared of you, don't even bother coming back.
Aviaks are still very suspicious of you. As for me, I don't even want to look at you.

Those aviaks hold their grudges. We've done so much for them, and all that work was nearly flushed down the drain over one stupid... erm, let's call it accident. If the aviaks believe it, so will I. Watch out, though - don't let it happen again.
Bring 10 Parrot Feathers and 10 Cornelians to Koati Close-Lipped.

The war continues. I've live a long time, and always seen war. Young or old, everyone takes a sword in a paw and goes for battles and arrows. An arrow always knows who to hate and hit. Its target will lay in a cold ground.
I do not know a remedy for war, but I know a remedy for arrow. I can make a talisman and every arrow will miss, not touching feather, not cutting skin, not sticking in the body. I just need good feathers and right stones. But I'm old, and there are wild jungles behind the settlement. Will Son of the Wind help me? Look - this is a good feather, which an arrow will recognize and won't hit, flying to the side. Take it from a parrot. This is a proper stone, it's bright, making an arrow less angry, so that an arrow won't wound the body. Find it in the gravel. Ten feathers, ten stones - ten young warriors come home from battle.
Will the day come when I see no war anymore?
Good. Give me stones and feathers. Now it's time for a spell. Karmaram-marakarm, heart's not sad, bird flies away, arrow misses far, karraki-nag-marra...
Defeat Wandering Hevea and return the lost axe to the Twiggy family.

When we were little, we read a book about a postman. He was cast away on a deserted allod, where he had to survive on the junk in the parcels. He was a clever dude, though - he crafted an axe from a pair of skates and made fire with mana batteries. He even pulled out a bad tooth with a rune-extracting rod... hurts me just thinking about it. Who knew we would ever find ourselves in a similar mess?
At least our teeth are fine, praise Tensess. Although we did lose our axe... What will we use to cut wood now? And not a pair of skates in sight!
But it's our own fault. We went for a branch in the dark, didn't realize it was a treant's leg! His sap was so sticky that the axe got stuck, and now the creature is walking around with our axe in its leg! We barely managed to escape with our lives, else the treant would have made leather gloves out of us!
Could you find him for us? Don't go alone, though, he's a big one, not just some old stump. Get some of your tougher friends to help, and we will make it worth your while.
What could I use to make a new axe? Knives? Too small. A ship fragment? Too long a walk. A battle axe? Where could we get one?
Thanks so much! It's a bit rusty, but that's all right - we'll clean it up.
Question Phell about the circumstances of his death.

Gracious sir, may I steal a few minutes of your precious time? I have an incredibly important matter for your consideration. I am one of the guerillas fighting to oppose the tyranny of the architect of these dreams, so to speak. Do forgive me, I can't tell you my name right now, but the Resistance calls me the Ghost.
Our common friend sent you to look for holes in the fabric of this amazing illusion. Your search has already been interrupted twice by extraordinarily curious, albeit frightening creatures. Let us call them Lictors. They are the executioners of the master who has woven the fabric of this delusion, and he does not want his creation to be ripped by those caught in it. Within the boundaries of this illusory world they can wield any power that their creator endowed onto them.
It would seem that they are invincible, wouldn't it? That may be, but let me draw your attention to a rather curious paradox. To protect the fabric of reality from holes, even a concocted reality, they must be interwoven in it themselves. That means that, by virtue of their service, they are restricted by the rules and laws of this world... It follows that they must also have a certain weakness.
There is just one thing left to do, a simple little thing - find that weakness and learn to use it against them. Let's pull on the only thread that we have. Question that poor aviak about how he was possessed by a Lictor. Perhaps his story will give us a clue.
I'm guilty before Son of the Wind. I know that wingless one has no blame, but stayed silent. I beg forgiveness. An I'll tell the truth.

I am a coward. Everyone blamed you, Son of the Wind, and I had not courage to oppose the tribe. Now brothers are calm and can talk.
When you fought, I heard a strange sound, like a broken wind. Sparks in the eyes, muddled mind... I saw and remembered everything, but my body did not obey. I saw my hands beat Son of the Wind by themselves. Now do you understand why I stay quiet? I can't say that to brothers, they won't believe. Either they will believe that I am a liar, or that I'm possessed by an evil spirit. Now it's gone, but what if the tribe knows, what if the tribe becomes scared and banishes me?
One last thing. You have no blood of mine on your hands. My life was cut short by the evil spirit, not a weapon. I am sorry and ask your forgiveness.
Well, what did the aviak say? Are there any other... clues, if you will?
Find Silvia de Vevre's expedition in the Hills.

It is just as I thought. The Architect didn't damage his creation by introducing strange unbeatable creatures. Instead, he carefully wove them into the fabric of his creation as evil spirits. They manipulate events by putting up obstacles in the saboteurs' path, while keeping the world's logic unharmed. Though the spirits themselves are naturally bodiless, they still have a presence. They leave behind traces, if you will. For a capable seer, tracking them is no more difficult than tracking a forest animal is for an experienced hunter.
I recall that there were three highly talented seers in that expedition team. If memory serves me right, they are called the Brainiac family. At the moment they have gone off to the Hills with the sorceress Silvia de Vevre. Of course, you realize that this matter is no less important. I recommend that you find the expedition and ask for help before you encounter another Lictor, or worse...
Oh, you are right on time!
Use the bioenergetic crystal to make aura clones of Alk Two-Arrows, Phell Sharp-Sighted and Koati Close-Lipped, then return the crystal to the Brainiac Family in the League Settlement.

We committed a serious error with that expedition. Everyone is avoiding Silvia now. What on earth got into us... Oh well, it's all over now. Nobody was hurt, and that's the main thing. Was there something you wanted to discuss?
So, there is an evil spirit around? That's not good... though not so scary, either.
We'll need the evil spirit's aura clone to catch him. We had some possessed around here, didn't we? Oh, just one? That's enough, we'll just have to work a bit harder. Thing is, we don't specialize in aviak auras, so we'll need several samples.
Here's a crystal for you - it's new, virginally pure and bioenergetic. Give it to the possessed fellow to hold, and his aura will imprint on the crystal, along with the imprint of the evil spirit. But that's not enough, we'll also have to split them up somehow. For that we'll need imprints of aviaks' pure auras, the ones that haven't been affected by the evil spirit. To make it easier for us, make sure that one of them is the same age as the possessed, while the other is a bit older. When you obtain all three clones, bring the crystal to us. We'll identify the evildoer.
Be careful, don't break the crystal! We have less than two boxes of them left.

Let's have a look. Oh, I see, that's our martyr. Look at that - a clear imprint, a strong trace of another's influence. The second... There, we can see a trace of something alien too, but very faint - they were probably in contact with the possessed. The third one is pure aviak. So that's what they're really like! Now we just need to isolate the spirit's aura and we are done. One second...
We have four imprints here. Where did the fourth one come from? Guess! You, obviously! But that's not the curious part. The curious part is this: why is the evil spirit's aura so similar to yours?
Extract 15 portions of poison from blacklip snakes with your knife and bring them to Alk Two-Arrows.

I believe that Son of the Wind doesn't mean to. Sparring match can still be match, even old warrior's hand can slip, not moving sword fast enough. I'm old, I see many things and know lots about war. But a young warrior's like baby chick, not understands much. Son of the Wind, know this - they look on wingless one with respect and fear, they do not believe that you can make mistake.

Son of the Wind caused wound, now you must also help heal. Red-winged and wingless allies are strong, lots of attacks and injuries, but I'm lacking the healing balm. I need snake poison for balm. Go to forest, find the snake and kill it. Then be careful. Use this knife, cut it under tongue and drain poison. Don't drip on yourself, it's very dangerous! Bring me one dozen and three poison portions. Everyone will see how Son of the Wind cares for tribe, works for white wings' mission!
This poison be like mature warrior. Can kill, can save.
Son of the Wind work quickly, good hunter be, aviaks watch and learn. Alk see that Wingless go hunting often.
Collect 15 resilient branches from tropical treants and give them to Lada Vereskova. Then distribute 5 bows among the white-winged troopers.

I've never met archers quite as good as these locals. Just you look at what they are shooting from! It takes extraordinary skill to hit even a century-old oak with a bow of primitive stick-and-rope construction, let alone a moving target. It literally pains me to watch them struggle with that junk. If only we could give them something more practical than this sacred traditional ugliness...

Meanwhile, I'll make the bowstrings. To be safe, bring as many branches as you can. Even in skilled hands, branches have a tendency to break two times out of three.
I just saw some feathered super-genius shoot a bow with his feet. The funny part is that he hit the mark! If only they learn to do things properly, they would be unbeatable.

I am completely stunned. Our aviaks really liked the bows. They flew by, thanked us, praised the precision of the bows. But an hour later they were back playing with their old stick-and-rope weapons. Supposedly all the new bows broke. Or were lost. What do you call that, eh? Stubborn acts out of spite or plain old sabotage? We need to try and re-equip them again. When the Empire comes, these mighty birds will feel like helpless quails for all the good their tradition will do them.
Bring 10 parrot feathers and 10 cornelians to Koati Close-Lipped.

The war continues. I've live a long time, and always seen war. Young or old, everyone takes a sword in a paw and goes for battles and arrows. An arrow always knows who to hate and hit. Its target will lay in a cold ground.
I do not know a remedy for war, but I know a remedy for arrow. I can make a talisman and every arrow will miss, not touching feather, not cutting skin, not sticking in the body. I just need good feathers and right stones. But I'm old, and there are wild jungles behind the settlement. Will Son of the Wind help me? Look - this is a good feather, which an arrow will recognize and won't hit, flying to the side. Take it from a parrot. This is a proper stone, it's bright, making an arrow less angry, so that an arrow won't wound the body. Find it in the gravel. Ten feathers, ten stones - ten young warriors come home from battle.
Will day come when Koati see time without war?
Good! Give stones, give feathers. Only spell left. Karmaram-marakarm, heart not sad, bird fly away, arrow miss far, karraki-nag-marra...
Rescue the missing Brainiac family and report to Silvia de Vevre in the Hills.

Well, at least somebody came! I was near the end of my tether!
Those gibberlings are nothing but trouble! They are adults, but they act like children! We barely managed to pitch camp, hardly had we made a fire when those maddening Brainiacs shouted that they were going on a scouting mission and disappeared! Come on, what scouting mission?? The League Camp is a stone's throw away, what is there to scout? They might have at least told a white lie, that they went to chop wood or something...
Instead, here I am, wasting the day waiting for them to come back, but they're nowhere in sight! What am I supposed to think? Maybe their bones have already been digested by crocs! What a marvelous start to the expedition, just great!
Can you do something for me? Please find those furry rogues. They must be somewhere nearby. Grab them by the ears and drag them back here!
And these are supposedly the League's best psionicists! They are so infantile.

Let's sum up the expedition's achievements thus far... Two of the participants were nearly eaten. One stuffed his face full of frogs, and another one has completely lost faith in humanity, especially in its furry members. I think that we can officially concede our failure. Now let's break camp and go home.
Collect 15 Cardamom Flowers in the Hills and bring them to Silvia de Vevre.

In the interest of full disclosure, before we were forced to look for our lost companions, the main goal of our expedition was collection of rare plants for alchemical potions. I fear we don't have time for that anymore, but I can't just go back empty-handed, right?
I've noticed that there is some kind of spicy herb growing around the camp. According to this field guide, I think it's cardamom. It doesn't grow in our altitude, and what a pity - its properties are perfectly suited for a particularly valuable potion.
Unfortunately, I am a scholar, not a fighter. There are monsters in these woods, and all of my tough guys have run off in search of adventures. Please be so kind as to collect ten flowers for my experiments. Better yet, make that 15.
By the way, cardamom is an excellent spice. Although we probably should test this variety for toxicity...
Thank you! Well, at least the day wasn't completely wasted.
Bring 10 Yeti Fangs, 10 pieces of Spider Chitin and 10 portions of Mind-Blowing Slime to Silvia de Vevre.

There's just one thing in this tropical paradise that concerns me. Now, this might sound a bit strange to you, but something about this is just wrong. I don't want to talk like I'm paranoid, but my gut feeling tells me that there is something... unnatural... in these woods. It's hard to explain it, but... well, just look at these two bushes. They are exactly the same! Down to the last vein of the last leaf! How can that be?
I don't want to scare anyone with fears I can't prove, but I can't carry out all the necessary research by myself. I beg you to obtain some samples of local fauna for my tests. Let's start with yeti fangs. I couldn't see very well through the binoculars, but it seemed to me that they were carefully dented in the same spot. I would like to compare ten samples from different specimen. Second, spiders. Did you know that the patterns on spider chitin shells are as unique as human fingerprints? Bring me ten chitin shells for my research. And finally, river toads. I believe they resemble a rare poisonous sub-genus. I will need some samples of their venom. Ten will be more than enough.
Pardon? What does the toad venom have to do with anything? Never mind that, I don't have time to explain and you wouldn't understand anyway.
The samples! Thank you! Hmm... See, even through a regular magnifying glass it's quite clear that they are identical! I'll have to check them under the microscope.
Carry Ubbi Brainiac to Silvia de Vevre at the expedition camp.

"High in the clouds flies a black-winged aviaaaaaak... Trembling and lonely, yet somehow he soars..."
The gibberling is rambling. His eyes have rolled back, his fur is soaked with sweat and he's surrounded by piles of dead toads, all of which bear teeth marks. You don't have to be a great detective to figure out that the seer decided to add some spice to his mystical visions and licked a whole bunch of hallucinogenic toads. Let's just hope that their slime is not too poisonous. And the frog licker should be taken to Silvia de Vevre. She is a biologist, she'll think of something.
Well, have you found those furry scoundrels?

Just you look at that! What a hero! He said that he was going on a scouting run, and instead he waged a war between mice and toads! What am I to think! Bring that psychonaut here, I'll have him back to his senses and send him back to the village in a flash. In the meantime go and find the rest of them.
Kill 10 Forest Yeti in the Hills and report to Bosi Brainiac.

Who's there?! Ah, friends? Phew, we... I was so scared.
We pitched camp, left Silvia to look after it and went on a scouting mission. We've never seen forests like this! Trees! Grass! And all this after Siveria! We were watching birdies and didn't even notice going into a clearing full of those damned yiti... yetiti... yeeeti... Those monsters! We ran as hard as we could, obviously. And now we... I am sitting here, wondering where my brothers have gone, whether or not they are alive?
Oh, you're already searching for them? Thanks! Well, help get me out of here! We are not the worst psionicists, honest... false modesty aside. But only when we are together! Alone I'm but a single mouthful for those yetiti... monsters! Why don't you distract them by killing a dozen or so? That'll clear the way for me to make a run for it! Can you do that?
If we hadn't dispersed, we would've scorched those furry beasts' brains right out! But alone I can't even think straight. I start a thought, but there is nobody to continue it.
Thank you! I'm off! Go and find my brothers, please. Let's meet back in the settlement and talk there.
Return to Fafni Brainiac his belongings, stolen by spiders: Diary of Dreams, Psionicist Helmet, Psionicist Rod and Oracle Tablet.

Help! Help!
Oh... Thanks, I almost chocked to death in this cobweb! How did we manage to... Hang on, where are my brothers? Oh, you're searching for them already? Phew, that's a load off my mind. I think... Actually, no, it's not. Make sure to find them, eh? I beg you in the name of holy Tensess.
Well, shall we go? Stop! Those spiders are so fast! They didn't just catch me, they emptied my pockets too! Just you look at them! Everything we've have accumulated through hard and honest labor... gone, all gone! A legendary rod that we've spent so many amalgams on! A psionicist helmet, handmade, with crystals! A dream diary with all our secrets! An oracle tablet that we'd used just this morning to foresee its loss! Why would spiders need these things?
I doubt that those bugs had time to drag them too far. Have a look around the cave - I'm sure that our treasures are hidden in their cocoons. And try not to forget anything, lest my brothers get so mad they'll bash my head in!
Well, at least they didn't steal our gold and gems.
Thank you! It's all in place, now I'll just have to clean off the spider webs. Please look for my brothers while I go back to the settlement. See you there!
Report Silvia de Vevre's words to Voibor Ratov in the League Camp.

Well, it's time to wrap up. Won't you help us break our camp? Oh, you are in a hurry... I understand. Oh well. Fair enough, not every Elvish maiden can hope for a valiant knight at her side...
Oh, and another thing. Since you are in such a hurry to get back to the camp, take this with you. I don't know about our wanna-be scouts, but I actually did see someone interesting while waiting for the Brainiacs' return. A small and furry critter wandering outside the camp. At first I thought that it was one of my companions, but then I saw it. I don't know what it was, but I can say for certain that it was no gibberling. I wanted to get a closer look but then it just ran off, leaving behind some orange peel. It's nowhere to be found at this point, but you should report it to Voibor Ratov just in case. Let him do something about it, I don't know... like double the camp sentries or whatever. Now go. I will break camp and carry the tents back to the settlement by myself. I hope I don't get eaten by some tropical monster on the way back. Come on, go already! Weren't you in a hurry a minute ago?!

I get it. Let me get this straight. Silvia saw something she didn't recognize, the creature ran away in a direction she didn't see, and now she wants me to do something about it. Now this is what I call valuable information!
Find the reality distortion in Muggy Jungle. Summon Lictor and defeat it with the Spear of Truth.

What a spear! It's almost radiating strength. You could hunt Octulhu with it, never mind some random evil spirit!
Here, take the detector. We've approximately located our bogey - it's sitting in the Muggy Jungle. You'll have to look for the lair, but it'll hardly be tough: the reality is well distorted around it. When the evil spirit gets close, press this tumbler and he will be yanked into the real world! But you won't be able to defeat him just like that - regular weapons and even combat magic will only wear it out. So when he gets tired, that's your chance - thrust the spear right between the eyes, or whatever he's got on his head! Anyway, this is your domain much more so than ours.
Just be careful. Don't let him make you his food.
Fantastic! Truly, nothing can stop someone who believes in himself!

So, you've managed to obtain... well, to create... a weapon capable of destroying the elite servants of Tep - the Lictors. Congratulations! What do you think has really defeated your enemy? The logic of the world, perhaps the rules of the game that he must obey? Correct. But that's just one side of the truth.
Do you remember what you had to do to acquire this spear? You've passed some kind of test, haven't you? You have shown the will to win, so to speak, by opposing oblivion. That's why this spear is more than just some imagined toy in the illusory world. In a manner of speaking, this weapon is the manifestation of your will to live. If my theory is correct, it will remain with you in the real world, where it will just as dangerous to the architect of dreams as it is here.
Bring 8 Astral Monocrystals from the abandoned mine to the Brainiac family in the League Settlement.

OK, listen up. We worked out that this spirit's aura is very similar to yours in many respects. Wait, let me finish! It's similar to our auras, too, and everyone else's for that matter. Everyone except the aviaks. That means that this spirit is as much of an alien here as we are. Perhaps he isn't even a spirit, but... well... Who knows what he is! Let's save the questions for when he's in our hands. Then we'll know who he is, where he came from and why he's bullying the birdies.
We already have an aura clone and most of the parts for the detector, and what we don't have can easily be welded. The only thing we're missing are crystals for the amplifier. I suppose we could grow them, but that will take months... Don't fret, there is another way.
Our scouts spotted a mine with native crystals in the southeastern part of the island. It's very ancient, probably built by Junes. Our scouts didn't go inside though - they were scared of the elementals who live there. But you're not the frightened type, are ya? Gather eight crystals for us while we collect everything else.
Well, will you be getting us some crystals, or should we start priming a barrel to grow them in?

Wow! They are so big and pure and translucent! With filling this good, we could build a working detector out of copper coins, a broken wire and an old boot! Now give us a minute to finish building it.
Now remember, the detector will help you find the evil spirit, but it won't be of any use in combat. So while we're welding it together, go and find a weapon that can take the spirit down. Sorry, but we won't give you the device until you arm yourself properly. Otherwise, finding that creature is the last thing you need!
Kill 20 Stone Elementals in the abandoned mine and report to Voibor Ratov in the League Camp.

There is an old abandoned mine full of native crystals in the southern part of the island. The Historians would probably like to know who built it and when, since for our aviaks a simple cube is a wonder of technology. But that's the Historians. We, however, are interested in something else - how to appropriate it before the Empire does.
Our scout reported about a trail that runs to the mine. It's old but fairly clear and without any serious obstructions, not counting a river crossing and tapirs that graze near the entrance. There are plenty of untouched crystals in that mine. There is just one problem - stone elementals have made their home there. If you liquidate them, the minerals will be ours.
Well, is the mine clear? Can we dispatch our workers there?
Not bad. I see now that you can work hard, not just talk about Tep.
Bring 20 Tapir Skins to Koati Close-Lipped.

Many young chicks think magic can do anything. Few young chicks think magic is lies. Both are stupid. Magic works well when the head works well and does not forget important things. How can anyone protect from wounds? Use a talisman? Of course! What else? Armor! Young chicks scoff at armor, want to be heroes, but believe in talismans. I'll make a talisman.
Powerful animals wander near mine. It's hard to break through their skin, and hard to kill them. Strip their hides and put it on feathers - it will be strong protection for aviaks! are you laughing? I weep when foolish chicks go look for valor and return with no head.
Help me protect young chicks. Bring one dozen and three thick hides.
Magic works simple. Eat jaguar heart and become brave. Eat tapir nose and grow a big beak, look handsome for ladies. You should try, growing a nice beak!

The hide is strong, very good. Two dozens of young chicks will come home safe. Be attentive, if you meet a smart animal in the woods, then tell me. If I feed a smart animal's brain to the tribe, I'll make them smart!
Return to Kahlua Island and ask Elchana how to defeat the evil spirit.

An evil spirit cannot be seen by eyes, touched by hands, hit by arrows, nor cut by swords. But there must be a special weapon! Do you know Elchana Speak-with-Spirits? She's an old wise witch, knows everything. Go to Elchana, who sees spirits, talks spirits, knows a remedy against spirits!
Son of the Wind has come again... White is your face, worry is in your heart. I know how to help.
Kill 15 Pagan Aviaks or Agitators of the Trinity Church, then report to Elchana Speak-with-Spirits on Kahlua island.

Now this s-s-s-spear can banish the spirits of lies-s-s-s... Jus-s-s-s-t have to prove that you des-s-s-serve to own it. Show me, s-s-s-s... how you des-s-s-troy your enemies-s-s-s. If I like this-s-s, I will give you the power which will des-s-s-stroy all your enemies-s-s-s in this world...

Everyone want believe that he be on side of truth and his enemy not be. But there be only one truth in war between Glittering Wing and Steel Claw, as in war between League and Empire - you truly hate and want destroy each other. That be not scary. That be like the way our world go, driven by fighting.
Son of the Wind, prove your power to fix what is broken. I'll give you, Son of the Wind, this spear. Go and banish broken spirits.
Ask the Brainiac Family in the League Settlement for help.

Now the warriors are armed! But can a warrior see? Does a warrior know how to find enemy, how to sneak up to him, how to strike? Evil spirit is slippery, untouchable like smoke and shadows.
You need help to fight the spirit of falsehood. Not mine, no - you already know the one who can help, you arrived on the same ship! Three hearts beat as one, three minds shine as one. Return to them, ask for help. They will give you the sight!

Please, please tell me - how do these woodland healers always know everything? Other people have to work, study, read books, do research in laboratories, but all they get is more questions and doubts. Meanwhile, some old hag who has never stepped foot outside her wood barely shrugs her feathers and lo and behold - she knows everything about us... Oh well. An evil spirit detector, eh? Of course we can help.
Talqua toock quarr, Son of the Wind! I talk with Wind Spirits, they bless our union!
Find Ulk Blitz-Beak near the Sunny Cascade.

What happened to the aviak? He's been gone a long time, but we haven't heard any screams or sounds of battle. Maybe he broke his back carrying all those stones? They are birds, after all. They are proud, but their bones are fragile. We ought to help him...
Do me a favor and go find him. His name is Ulk Blitz-Beak. Evidently, it's not just Novograd guards that get blitzed on the job. In the meantime, we'll... We'll look after the lift for a while, make sure that nothing else falls off.
The aviak is motionless but appears to be breathing.
My whole body hurts... Thank you, Son of the Wind! If you did not find me, I could have flown to the Empyreal Grove.
Bring 6 stones to the elevator and report to the Floppers family.

Wingless people are brave warriors, but all is in vain. Bad luck they have, very bad. No luck in hunt, no luck in battle. As they sit on the platform, the rope has broken right away! They should stay in their village, weaving baskets. They almost died, a big boulder broke the car, almost hit and killed me. That stone cannot be hung again, it's bad luck. We need lots of new stones, full of fresh strength from mother Earth.
But my luck is no good either. In the past, I used to fly here all over, not afraid of anything. Suddenly, a poisonous finguses started crawling out and bit my paw! Then there were more and more of them! I ran away, but the poison was bad, very bad... it made my eyes dark, I could not breathe and fell over... Fingus' poison does not kill. It's not a good death for a warrior - to lie down with no memory, and wait for a wild animal to chew his face.
I'm still weak, I can't move and my wings feel numb. I need rest. But the time does not wait, a big war is all around. You're strong, and you have luck. Can you find new stones for the elevator and tie a new load? Then a new lift will work for ninety nine moons without a break!
Be careful, don't strain yourself. We'd help, but Ulk forbade us - he says that we'll infect the stones with bad luck. Maybe it's true? Alas...
Oh, look at that, it's working! Go ahead, we... erm... we'll follow, I guess.
Use the elevator to get up to the Windy Hills and report on your arrival to Voibor Ratov.

The elevator's working, that's great. Hey, why don't you go ahead without us. With our luck the load will probably crash again, or the basket will break, or some carnivorous palm tree will grow at the top. Do you know the way? It's not far. Report to Voibor Ratov when you arrive, he'll fill you in.
Hmm, what do we have here? Reinforcements? That's great, you are right on time. The relationship between the tribes has become super tense.
The lift does not look safe, but there is no other way...
Kill 15 Wild Azaleas and Rosebay and report to the Floppers Family.

I've thought it all over many times. Maybe some small furry warrior brings bad luck, but why so many finguses? Why do they all attack the same time? Bushes used to grow in peace, small animal chewed them. When teasing a frail warrior, we say: "You're so weak, a bush can bite you!" What happened?
I am an elevator keeper, so I'm responsible. What if an old, wounded or sick person needs to go up, and can't deal with the biting bush? I'm still sick from poison, can't hold a sword well... Do a good thing, help me! Destroy all vile plants, stalk and all!
First a shipwreck, then a lift-wreck, and now an invasion of poisonous plants... If we return home in one piece, we'll never go seeking adventures again. With our luck, we're better off staying home.

Still, it's a pity about these flowers, they are so pretty. We don't have flowers like that in Coldberg... But that's all right - in this jungle you turn away for a moment and new plants will have already replaced the old!
Find out who fed the poisonous finguses up and report to Voibor Ratov in the League Settlement.

I see. Empty bottle. Stinks of fertilizer. This is obviously not just any old manure, and not even a rapid growth elixir.
That's why there are man-eating fingus blooming near the lift: someone has grown them! I wonder who it was? Just need to find the source of the stink...
What's that bottle you've got? Oh, I see! And where did these gardening enthusiasts come from, I wonder? Go find out!

What you are witnessing is the price of Imperial hospitality! I just knew that all these talks of peace were just pure... fertilizer. Top grade! And we fell for it! Hook, line and sinker... Now we have to clean it up.
Return to the real world and tell Klavdia Kalugina about your victory over the lictor.

So, you have disrupted our enemy's plan in the most spectacular fashion: by beating him in his own game. I must say, not everyone is so capable. This gaping rift, if I can call it that - a fresh wound in the flesh of our illusory world - is clear confirmation of your success. I reckon this is the best time to return to the real world, however depressing it may be, to inform our common friend about our victory. As for me, do forgive me but I have some important unfinished work here. I will follow you as soon as I've finished my affairs. Until we meet again!

Not bad! Could it be that one of the "Chosen" on Gipat didn't listen to what the Dragons and Wormfaces were talking about? This spear is a very serious object, especially if you've managed to take it with you into the real world. I think I know what we can...
Wait, stop! What was that again? What Ghost? Can you describe him again? Right. Crap on a cracker...
There are no party members with the alias "Ghost". In fact, if you didn't notice, we don't use any party aliases at all. I did send a messenger, but he was intercepted by Lictors midway there. So who was it?

Obtain a Deadtree branch in the Hills, a shard of rock elemental in the Mine, and a Large Rhino's Tail on the Cape of Chiefs, then bring them to Elchana Speak-with-Spirits on Kahlua island.

When the world appeared, it was quiet and clean, like a lake. First aviaks sang, their voices united into one choir. But one, may his name be forgotten, thought that his voice was not heard. He sang louder. Then louder still. Then pulled his neighbor's feathers and he missed the note. A song was interrupted, like a calm lake covered in ripples, then ripples created waves, and waves became storm. This storm is lies. Evil spirits are made from lies, not flesh and bone. One can't destroy all lies, like you can't drink the entire sea. But an evil spirit can be driven away here and now. That is the purpose of the ritual. I will make a weapon of truth. I'll cast a spell, write the story of world's creation on that spear, enchant it with sacred truth. The spear will drive away the evil spirit dispersing lies.
The spear needs three powers. The power of a growing green - a branch of a walking tree. The power of the unshakeable earth - a shard of a walking stone. The power of the flesh and blood - a tail of a powerful beast. Go, bring them all and begin the ritual.
The spear won't go into a hand of the one who has lies in the heart. A liar's walking through dark, underground woods...
Stone, wood, flesh. Three powers, three lives, three allies. Now I'll make a weapon of truth.
